column8: Mon 16 Nov: 3d evidence; MoMA's figures checked at source (44,118 gross, 8,731 allowance, 3,021 discount, in thousands); these are the recipient's books, not a co-sponsor's, and 6.8 of the 27 cents is time, which her figure would also bear on the residency's books, so cite the 19.8% allowance for doubt, never 73 cents.

Mon 16 Nov: store; building-campaign pledges run years past opening and take the bigger cut; fix the use: the funds mature in December 2032 and the contribution is her 2033 contribution (case), so never say her figure is paid in December 2032.
Mon 16 Nov: the Met's 8.9% time cut against 2.1% doubt is already in row 9; only the 5.25% rate is extra.
Mon 16 Nov: store for 3d; a capital campaign makes pledges the largest new asset on a museum's books in one year (DMA 1.9m to 66.4m); one large museum, one year.

Mon 16 Nov: guard for 3d wording; audited zero allowances (MCASD, Tulsa, Cincinnati 0.15%) show an allowance is management's call, the audited form of Q53-021's 42%; it is why row 35 drops needs no allowance.
Mon 16 Nov: Broward's 18.5% time cut against 1.3% doubt is row 9's point; the 80-cent figure is Keel arithmetic on a component unit's note.

Mon 16 Nov: store for 3d; one small hall held 10.0% against capital pledges and 5.4% against annual ones; fix the use: never say her figure needs no such reserve (an allowance is the recipient's judgement, row 5), say it is owned before she states it.

Mon 16 Nov: 3d, gives a number to co-sponsors count the bottom, with two fixes: these are recipients' books (the residency's), never co-sponsors' own books; and most of the cut is time, which her figure would also take, so the contrast is the doubt allowance, 0% to 19.8% in nine statements read, never 73 to 98 cents against her Treasuries; a snapshot, not a sample.

Mon 16 Nov: guard for 3d; at a discount mostly means later, not doubtful (time beat doubt at LACMA, the Met, DMA, Broward, Akron, UNC), which is why row 8's contrast must use the allowance alone; carries rows 3 and 6.

Mon 16 Nov: 3d aha candidate; several charities discount pledges at a Treasury rate and then cut for doubt; fix two phrases: say several charities (MoMA and UF price the donor's risk into the rate, row 11), never every pledge; and never Laura's figure is a Treasury: it is her promise backed by Treasuries held for her, so ability is settled and willingness rests on the written form (Q18-027).

Mon 16 Nov: store; risk-adjusted discount rates are real (MoMA checked at source), but her credit is the Treasury's is false as said: the residency holds her promise, backed by Treasuries held for her; say her ability to pay rests on Treasuries.

Mon 16 Nov: store; pledges due within a year are booked at net realizable value; fix the date: the funds mature in December 2032 and the contribution is her 2033 contribution, so a figure stated before the 2031 meetings is more than a year out and takes a time discount either way.
Mon 16 Nov: store; the 39-cent deferred-gift book is Keel arithmetic on an excerpt whose foundation is not named; name the entity at source before any use, and most of its cut is time, not doubt.

Mon 16 Nov: 3d clause; an allowance is built from collection history, economic conditions and ability to pay, which for Laura is a checkable holdings statement (Q43-035); fix: it is the residency's auditor that would book her pledge, not a co-sponsor's, and willingness still needs the written form (Q18-027).

Mon 16 Nov: store for 3e outside funding; auditors flag one donor at 46% or 23% of a pledge book, so a small campaign rests on a few promises; university foundations, beside Q11b-031's campaign concentration.

Mon 16 Nov: 3e evidence for IPS l.15's a co-sponsor falling short; ASU Foundation's booked doubt rose from 3.6% to 30.7% in 2008-10; say can, never fall together; it is an accountant's estimate at one foundation, not measured collections.

Mon 16 Nov: store; the allowance stayed at 22-26% to 2018 and 13.2% in 2024, but the card cannot separate old from new pledges, so say only that it stayed above its 2008 level for a decade, never that the books still do not count the crisis pledges.

Mon 16 Nov: 3e honesty clause; no national statistics on unpaid pledges are kept (checked at source), so a co-sponsor's shortfall stays an assumption; adds the 2008 base and the 3.3 times rise to H7-070's Duke figure.

Mon 16 Nov: 3d, why the ask sets one total and one close date before building: failed pledges cost most where money was already spent (MTSU's pianos) and least before construction (the stadium pledge could be cancelled); quotes checked at source.

Mon 16 Nov: store; in 2009 Duke's donors favoured one-time gifts over multi-year pledges (a student newspaper quoting an official); co-sponsors' payment dates are not set by the plan, so never say a co-sponsor is asked for money at the end of 2032.
Mon 16 Nov: store for 3e; a dozen billion-dollar campaigns' collections fell 32% in a year as donors postponed; collections, not failed pledges, and the page is partly paywalled.

Mon 16 Nov: 3d counter-case beside row 23; donors with money already held paid early in April 2009; a downturn tests what backs a promise, which is the point of her figure being owned before she states it.

Mon 16 Nov: 3d or 3e, the plainest picture of spending on pledges: 92.6m counted, 58.6m received, agencies already spending on the pledged figure (checked at source); name both causes the source gives (economic problems and controversies), 63 cents is Keel arithmetic; one case beside the Taiwan reserve Q50-008, choose one for 3d.

Mon 16 Nov: 3d or 3e contrast with IPS l.17; a 1920s pledge card let donors cancel on financial reverses, where the IPS names two reasons and not a market fall; fix the use: such a pledge can lapse in the same downturn in which shares fall, never fails exactly when shares fall.

Mon 16 Nov: store for 3e; a firm written pledge raised follow-through from 23% to 36% at Danish doorsteps (checked at source; significant only at 10%); 45% refusing is the abstract's figure (about 40% in the body); small sums, not capital pledges.
Mon 16 Nov: a second measured follow-through rate, from a one-week laboratory test with 5 dollars; row 25's field test is the stronger home for the point.

Mon 16 Nov: enforceability of charitable pledges is H3-109 (Q18-028); the use overreaches: owned Treasuries settle her ability to pay, not her willingness, so they do not spare a residency a court (Q18-027).

Mon 16 Nov: 3d; FASB's own example of a condition is a like amount raised from others within 30 days, and a matching grant is a common conditional promise (both checked at source); the accounting form of Q18-007's CASE rule for the ask's one total and one close date.

Mon 16 Nov: 3d, explains the ask's order: on US rules a co-sponsor pledge made conditional on the total books nothing until the total is met, while her figure stated unconditionally is booked when stated; Keel inference, and a Taiwan residency may not follow US rules, so say on US rules.
Mon 16 Nov: store for 3d; FASB's museum-wing example makes milestone-paid building pledges conditional whatever their likelihood (checked at source); her contribution is tied to no milestone.

Mon 16 Nov: store guard for 3d; booking is not law (BC39) and boilerplate return clauses do not make a condition (BC31), so never call her figure a legal pledge; BC31 and BC39 not rechecked by this rater.
Mon 16 Nov: commitment words decide booking (Q18-004), the case's verb expects is Q77-002 and ambiguity presumed conditional is Q18-003; FASB's will example is the only addition.
Mon 16 Nov: store for 3d; auditors show conditional pledges in a note, not in the total (MoMA's 5,000 thousand checked at source); the practice behind row 29.

Mon 16 Nov: store; GASB foundations book endowment pledges only as cash, but the use is false: under a cash-only rule her figure also counts only when paid, so never say her owned figure passes the strictest form; say a public co-sponsor may count some promised money only as cash.

Mon 16 Nov: 3d wording guard, restating Q7c-035 and Q73-031's note (owned before stated, never needs no allowance); fix: drop the one promise, since a donor with cash in hand may also pledge (row 22); say her figure is owned before she states it and unconditional when stated, and that it takes a time discount on the residency's books.

Mon 16 Nov: 3c and 3d, restates SKELETON 3d's what can lower it; NUMBERS gives about $119 off the top per 0.1% of costs above the cut (Sun 15 Nov evening), not $120; and the funds' costs are not one of IPS l.17's two reasons, so keep the two lists apart.
